_directive: losslessly compressed, token-efficient, information-dense, fully detailed, machine-facing; optimized for model parsing over human readability
generated_by: orchestrator (Phase B seed; deep population deferred to helpers like Phase A.2)
grain_decision: one dense KB per SUBDOMAIN (subdomain grain), per Phase A calibration; rich subdomains may split to TOPIC grain at build time per kb_generation_job grain rule
consulted: Phase A Knowledge Searcher router (specialists/ROUTER.json) is queried per-subdomain to locate authoritative sources before generation
real_world_execution_notes: The SCIENCE underneath (probability, methodology, cognition, IR/KR, evaluation theory) is book-stable and largely covered by Phase A's find/evaluate specialists.

The EXECUTION of this system is frontier/tacit: it lives in model cards, framework docs (TRL, PEFT, Axolotl, Unsloth, vLLM, DeepSpeed, llama.cpp, LangGraph, Outlines), public leaderboards (Open LLM Leaderboard, LMSYS Arena, HELM), vendor GPU pricing, and base-model LICENSES/ToS — and it shifts monthly. Each domain tags this in frontier_not_in_books.

Hard real-world constraints to encode as KB conflict_axes/dominance_rules: (a) base-model license/ToS limits what you may legally fine-tune/serve; (b) small fine-tuned specialists beat generalists only on NARROW, well-specified tasks, not broad 'thinking'; (c) orchestration multiplies latency+cost per hop; (d) benchmark scores are contaminated/gameable (Goodhart); (e) safety-layer ablation degrades general capability and breaks hosted-model ToS.

Empirical lesson the user cited (raw-data biomedical model beating curated specialists): favor representative/raw training data + verifiable reward over hand-picked bookish examples; treated as a data-curation dominance rule in D1.
